name: Chouine
description: Chouine is a traditional French trick-taking card game played mainly in and around the Loire Valley. It is primarily a two-player game, though adaptations for 3 or 4 players exist. The game combines trick-taking with declarations of combinations (marianna) that determine trumps and score bonus points. An annual Chouine World Championship is held in Lavardin.

rules.objective: Score card points by winning tricks containing valuable cards (brisques) and by declaring combinations (marianna). Win the partie by reaching the target score first. A complete game consists of the best of three manches.
rules.gameplay:
1. Deal 5 cards to each player, remainder forms talon
2. Turn top card of talon for trump indicator
3. Player holding 7 of trumps may exchange it for the trump indicator
4. Play consists of series of parties (deals)
5. Each partie: Players play cards, may declare marianna (K+Q of same suit)
6. First marianna declared sets trump suit and scores 40 points
7. Later mariannas score 60, 80, 100 points but may or may not change trump
8. Winner of last trick scores extra 10 points (dix de der)
9. Total points per partie: 130 (cards) + 10 (last trick) + possible marianna points
keyRules: No obligation to follow suit initially (until trump is established)
First marianna declared establishes trump suit
Marianna consists of King and Queen of same suit held in hand
Player with 7 of trumps can exchange it for trump indicator
Winner of trick draws first from talon, then opponent
After talon exhausted, must follow suit if possible
If cannot follow suit, must play trump if possible
Dix de der: 10 bonus points for winning last trick

strategy.basic: Learn the card values and marianna combinations. Try to capture Aces and Tens (brisques) in tricks. Declare mariannas when you have them.
strategy.intermediate: Since both players can declare combinations in any trick, there's no particular incentive to win tricks unless they contain valuable cards - except for the very last trick worth 10 extra points. In opening tricks, get rid of useless cards (7, 8, 9 of non-trump suits) and aim to collect combinations. When your hand consists only of 'useful' cards (brisques, kings, queens, jacks, low trumps), choose between trying to win tricks or declaring more combinations.
strategy.advanced: The holder of the 7 of trumps should always exchange it, but wait until ready to use the trump indicator card. Remember played cards - once a king or queen has been played, no further mariannas are possible in that suit. Use the tactic of 'fare morire in mano una marianna' - acting as though you have a marianna to discourage opponents from declaring theirs.
tips: The last trick (dix de der) is worth 10 points - plan for it
Exchange the 7 of trumps when you can use the indicator effectively
Track which kings and queens have been played
Early in a partie, discard low non-trump cards and collect combinations
Consider whether to declare marianna immediately or wait
Bluffing about having a marianna can be effective
